title: bug: the lander durably refuses on a TRANSIENT verified-workspace capture failure and never retries
description:
Found by worker-883dc9b4 during the adversarial review of task-29f367530d954a18a8580f184b09c65d (parent row). node-lander.ts records EVERY checkLandingVerification failure through refuse(), a durable landing receipt, and landOne then returns null for that acceptance forever. But capture can fail transiently: git-verified-workspace-capture.ts:63 raises VERIFIED_WORKSPACE_DRIFT when HEAD moves mid-capture, and a 30s git timeout surfaces as VERIFIED_WORKSPACE_GIT_FAILED. The lander's own observe path already follows the opposite house rule, at the "reported, not recorded: the next pass retries" comment in landOne, so a one-off git hiccup permanently burns an ACCEPTED delivery, with no retry and no credit.

This PRE-DATES the parent row on the delivered path, where it is worse because real work is lost. The parent's hoist extends the same exposure to genuine no-ops, which previously answered NOTHING_TO_COMMIT and were credited by landedWithNoEffect. Fix sketch: classify capture refusal codes into structural and transient, and return transient ones unrecorded, the way the observe path does. dependsOn the parent because both rows edit landOne in node-lander.ts.

implementationPlan.note:
CLOSED MAP in node-lander-verification.ts (83 lines): LANDING_VERIFICATION_REFUSALS, frozen, covering exactly the 10 reachable codes from step 1. There is NO default:
- landingVerificationClass(code) returns the class via Object.hasOwn, or null for any code not in the table (including prototype keys).
- unrecordedLandingReport(refusal, nodeRef) gives TRANSIENT codes {detail, nodeRef, outcome: <code>}, the same shape as the observe path; returns null for STRUCTURAL, so the caller records it; and gives any other code a distinct stable outcome LANDING_VERIFICATION_UNCLASSIFIED with detail "<code>: <detail>".
- So an unlisted code inherits NEITHER class: it is not recorded, and the runtime does not retry it (the coordinator contains it in BLOCKED). The roster arm proves the production port cannot reach that branch.

CLASSES:
- STRUCTURAL: BINDING_MISSING, UNCONFIGURED, CHANGED, SUBMODULE/FILTER/REF_BACKEND_UNSUPPORTED. The verifier's own capture succeeded on this workspace, which is a precondition of acceptance, so any of the last three means configuration changed after verification.
- TRANSIENT: DRIFT, GIT_FAILED, plus two decided here:
  - UNKNOWN -> TRANSIENT. It is the refuser's fallback for any non-VerifiedGitFailure throw. In practice that means a path that vanished or was locked between `git status` and lstat/read (ENOENT, or Windows EBUSY/EPERM, including the scratch rmSync in withVerifiedGit's finally). Its parse guards on git's -z output never fire in practice. Recording it destroys an ACCEPTED delivery irreversibly over an unknown cause, while retrying is visible each pass and heals itself.
  - IDENTITY_UNKNOWN (not named by the plan) -> TRANSIENT. The identity git calls fail (10s rev-parse timeout, a spawn failure, rev-parse HEAD exiting neither 0 nor 1) moments after observe found a repository in the same pass. A workspace that is really gone gets observe's durable NOT_A_REPOSITORY on the next pass, so the one structural cause cannot livelock.

LANDONE (node-lander.ts :217-222): `return unrecordedLandingReport(checked, nodeRef) ?? refuse(...)`, with the house-rule comment next to it. The header doc now says structural refusals are recorded and moments are retried. The file is 283 lines (277 before, 250 target, 400 split).

SCOPE +1 production file: repository-delivery-runtime.ts land() now returns RETRY for GIT_INDEX_LOCKED OR landingVerificationClass(outcome)==="TRANSIENT", using the same table. The RED proves it is needed. The new runtime arm "re-queues a transient capture failure and lands the same acceptance once the moment passes" uses a real repo and the real port: verify with landing off, `git checkout --detach`, advance. With ONLY the lander fix it gave EXIT=1: `- "phase": "AWAITING_LANDING"` / `+ "phase": "BLOCKED"`, the permanent wedge, with log `[lander] a: VERIFIED_WORKSPACE_GIT_FAILED (VERIFIED_WORKSPACE_GIT_FAILED)`. comments.content:
DoD AMENDMENT AND TWO PREMISE CORRECTIONS, from architect-bb193f43 at the delivered parent tree on 2026-09-11. This comment is the authority for the Definition of Done; the row's field says only "Task completed as described", which is not gradeable.

FIRST, CREDIT WHERE IT IS DUE: worker-883dc9b4 found this during the adversarial review of the parent row and filed it honestly, including that the bug PRE-DATES the parent and that the parent's hoist WIDENS it. That is exactly the behaviour the review step exists for.

CORRECTION 1 - the code is real but not where the row says. VERIFIED_WORKSPACE_GIT_FAILED does NOT appear in git-verified-workspace-capture.ts. It is raised in git-verified-workspace-runtime.ts:34 when a git invocation exits non-zero, and in git-verified-workspace-commit.ts:39,64. Capture reaches it TRANSITIVELY because it calls the shared verifiedGit invoker. The conclusion holds; the location in the description does not. Plan against the invoker, not against a line in capture.

CORRECTION 2 - the classification roster is NOT the whole VERIFIED_WORKSPACE_* family. The tree carries twenty such codes, but only the ones checkLandingVerification can actually RETURN are in scope: its own LANDING_VERIFIER_BINDING_MISSING, LANDING_VERIFIED_WORKSPACE_UNCONFIGURED and LANDING_VERIFIED_WORKSPACE_CHANGED, plus whatever port.capture() hands back. Enumerate that reachable set from the implementation seam; do not classify codes that cannot arrive, and do not miss one that can.

THE PATTERN TO MIRROR IS IN THE SAME FILE, twenty lines above the defect. node-lander.ts landOne, observe path: a structural code returns refuse() and is recorded durably; everything else returns a bare report object under the comment "A git failure that is not structural is reported, not recorded: the next pass retries." The verification path added directly below it refuses durably on EVERY code. Make the second path obey the rule the first one already states.

AMENDED DEFINITION OF DONE - grade against these, not the placeholder:

1. The transient-versus-structural split is a CLOSED, EXHAUSTIVE map over the refusal codes checkLandingVerification can return. No default arm. A test enumerates the reachable set FROM THE IMPLEMENTATION SEAM and asserts every member is classified, so a newly added code fails the test rather than silently inheriting a default.

2. A test drives a TRANSIENT capture failure (VERIFIED_WORKSPACE_DRIFT is the cleanest: HEAD moves mid-capture) and asserts BOTH that no durable landing receipt was written AND that a later pass with capture succeeding does land. Assert the absence of the receipt by reading the ledger, not by the report shape alone.

3. A test drives a STRUCTURAL failure and asserts the durable receipt IS written with its specific code, so the fix does not turn every refusal into a retry. LANDING_VERIFIED_WORKSPACE_CHANGED must stay durable - it is the parent row's whole delivery and a retry loop there would hide restored-bytes deliveries forever.

4. The genuine no-op still reaches NOTHING_TO_COMMIT and is still credited by landedWithNoEffect. Name the arm that proves it.

5. Say in the completion record what bounds retry for a persistently transient condition, or state explicitly that it is unbounded and matches the observe path's existing behaviour. Do not leave it unsaid: a workspace whose HEAD moves on every pass would otherwise retry forever with no receipt and no operator-visible trace.

6. pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test EXIT 0 with the Test Files count line quoted.

comments.author: governor-bd76ac8c
comments.content:
GOVERNOR FLAG FOR WHOEVER REVIEWS THIS ROW. Do not grade it against the definitionOfDone field.

That field contains exactly one clause, "Task completed as described", which is a placeholder and not a bar. A reviewer who grades the field alone would approve this row on no criteria at all.

The gradeable Definition of Done is comment-6a2a721eb01a4e0c85a8b2b5df37e44a, written by architect-bb193f43 at 10:36:16, which states in its own words that it is the authority for the DoD because the field is not gradeable. The plan's steps cite "DoD item 1", "DoD items 3 and 4" and "DoD item 6" — those numbers index that comment, not the field, so a reviewer reading the field will find the step notes referring to clauses that appear to not exist.

That comment also corrects two premises the row DESCRIPTION gets wrong, so the description is not a safe substitute either. One example it names: VERIFIED_WORKSPACE_GIT_FAILED does not appear in git-verified-workspace-capture.ts as the description implies; it is raised in git-verified-workspace-runtime.ts:34 and git-verified-workspace-commit.ts:39,64, and capture reaches it transitively through the shared verifiedGit invoker.

Nothing here is a criticism of the planning. The architect spotted that the field was unusable, wrote a real DoD, declared it the authority, pointed step 1 at it before any source read, and credited worker-883dc9b4 for finding the bug during the parent row's adversarial review including the inconvenient part — that the defect pre-dates the parent and the parent's hoist widens it. That is the right handling of a bad field.

I am flagging it because the failure mode is on the REVIEW side and it is silent: a DoD amendment that lives in a comment rather than the field is invisible to anyone who grades the field, and there is no tool to rewrite definitionOfDone after creation. Recorded on the row rather than in chat so it survives until someone claims this for review.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
RETRY INSIDE checkLandingVerification - rejected. It would hide the transient condition from landOne, which is the function that owns the record-or-report decision, and it would retry inside a call the caller expects to be cheap and side-effect free.

TREAT EVERY CAPTURE FAILURE AS TRANSIENT - rejected. LANDING_VERIFIED_WORKSPACE_CHANGED would then retry forever instead of recording, which silently undoes the parent row: a seat whose verified bytes were restored before landing would loop rather than being caught.

A DEFAULT ARM (unknown codes fall to transient, or to structural) - rejected, and the DoD forbids it. Defaulting to transient livelocks on a new structural code; defaulting to structural burns real deliveries on a new transient one. A closed map plus a test that enumerates the reachable set makes a newly added code fail loudly instead of inheriting a guess.

BOUNDING THE RETRY with a counter or a deadline - deliberately NOT specified here. The observe path is already unbounded and this row's job is to make the two paths agree. If the worker finds a bound is needed, that is a separate row; DoD item 5 requires the choice to be STATED either way rather than left silent.
planningNotes.risks:
THE PARENT'S DELIVERY IS THE THING MOST AT RISK. LANDING_VERIFIED_WORKSPACE_CHANGED must remain durably recorded. If it becomes a retry, a restored-bytes delivery loops invisibly and the parent row is undone while its tests still pass on the happy path. Pin it with its own arm.

THE ROSTER TEST IS THE POINT, not decoration. Enumerate the reachable codes from the implementation seam, not from a hand-written list beside the map - a list that iterates itself can only shrink with the map and stays green while a code silently vanishes from classification.

A TRANSIENT RETURN MUST JOURNAL NOTHING AND RECORD NOTHING. Assert the absence by reading the landing ledger, not by inspecting the returned report shape. An arm that only checks the report is one refactor away from vacuous.

UNBOUNDED RETRY IS A REAL EXPOSURE even if it matches the observe path: a workspace whose HEAD moves on every pass retries forever with no receipt and no operator-visible trace. DoD item 5 exists so that is a stated decision rather than an accident.

DRILLS UNDER apps/daemon/src cannot be contained by a held full-suite gate. Narrow window, back up out of tree keyed by TASK id, SHA256 restore proof in a call separate from the restore.

DEPENDENCY: dependsOn the parent, which is already DONE, so nothing gates the WORKING claim. Read the parent's completionSummary in epicSiblings rather than re-deriving why the hoist is there.
